verdict.rationale: pnpm documents per-project Node.js installation and pinning, driven by checked-in package.json fields: devEngines.runtime downloads Node.js, and packageManager / devEngines.packageManager switches the pnpm version on first use. The capability is limited to Node.js and pnpm itself, not language runtimes or tools in general. missing for 10: support for runtimes or tools beyond Node.js and pnpm, detailed config-file syntax docs for runtime pinning, independent or hands-on corroboration of per-project runtime switching.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install and switch language runtimes or tool versions per project from a checked-in config file

citations.quote: Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks, no “works on my machine” version mismatches.
Skip installing runtime entries (e.g. Node.js downloaded via `devEngines.runtime`).
If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use
Works as a Node.js version manager.
